purpose: Resolve the gauge branch left open by the smooth four-C4 twisted-orbit wire. For the explicit v7.7 positive control, refine the exact terminal orbit relation by the full relative S3 gain h_01=g_1^{-1}g_0. Prove that every accepted orbit pair has exactly one gain, so the gadget is a deterministic permutation on the full 18 local states (orbit type, gauge). Classify that permutation and show that an abstract network made only of this exact factor relation is solvable by linear-time propagation. Keep a strict source firewall: physically splicing the free Hamiltonian half-edges is not the same operation as identifying abstract terminal states and can add new colour inequalities.

exact_gain_refinement.global_symmetry_fix: Fix terminal-0 gauge g0=id and existentially quantify the two hidden orbit labels, both hidden gauges, and terminal-1 gauge g1.
exact_gain_refinement.S3_tuple_convention: A tuple p=(p0,p1,p2) is the colour permutation i->p_i; multiplication p*q means composition p after q.
exact_gain_refinement.rigidity: Conditioned on an accepted orbit pair, the relative terminal gain is a singleton. Hidden states still have four extensions, but none of that branching reaches the terminal gain interface.

full_state_transducer.map: F(tau,g)=(pi(tau), g * h(tau)^{-1}). Equivalently the factor enforces tau1=pi(tau0) and h(tau0)=g1^{-1}g0.
full_state_transducer.bijection: F is a permutation of all 18 local states; reversing the gadget uses F^{-1}.
sector_structure: For tau in {0,1}, pi swaps the orbit and h is the transposition (1 2), so F^2 is identity on all twelve states of this sector.
For tau=2, the orbit is fixed and h is the 3-cycle (0 1 2), so F has two three-cycles on the six gauge states.

abstract_network_terminal.model: Build a factor graph whose variable at each node is one Omega-state and whose oriented edge u->v imposes x_v=F(x_u); reversing edge orientation imposes F^{-1}.
abstract_network_terminal.algorithm: For each connected component choose one root. Try the at most 18 root states, propagate uniquely along a spanning tree, and verify every non-tree edge. This is O(18(|V|+|E|)) and reconstructs every accepted state assignment without branching in the graph size.
abstract_network_terminal.signed_cycle_exponent: For a closed walk, let k be the number of forward F traversals minus reverse F traversals. The root state must be fixed by F^k.
fixed_state_rule: The twelve tau in {0,1} states survive a cycle exactly when k is even.
The six tau=2 states survive a cycle exactly when k is divisible by 3.
Hence a connected identical-wire network is satisfiable iff either every fundamental-cycle exponent is 0 mod 2 or every fundamental-cycle exponent is 0 mod 3. Both conditions may hold simultaneously.

positive: The smooth v7.7 twisted orbit atom has no terminal gauge branching: it is an exact rigid S3 gain transducer.
Pure abstract networks of this one factor are not a hard three-state CSP; they reduce to a constant-state permutation-consistency problem and admit linear-time exact solve/reconstruct.
The order-six structure gives a compact potential/holonomy description instead of 18^n state enumeration.
killed: Treat the v7.7 twisted orbit wire itself as evidence of a hard finite-domain relation language.
Assume existential hidden gauge choices necessarily create terminal gauge branching in this positive control.
Enumerate gauge states independently at every factor in a network that really is only the exact F/F^{-1} permutation language.
firewall: The abstract-network terminal identifies complete terminal states. Actual source composition joins concrete dangling Hamiltonian vertices by new edges, which imposes additional NEQ constraints and is not proved equivalent to state identification.
The smooth hard source is therefore not solved by the order-six propagation theorem. Relation-preserving Hamiltonian completion remains mandatory.
The theorem concerns the displayed positive v7.7 control; it does not assert that all 32 four-C4 orbit-bijection openings have identical rigid gain lifts.
No SAT algorithm and no P=NP conclusion follows.

First enumerate two copies joined by all source-legal matchings of one terminal's three dangling vertices to the other's three dangling vertices, retaining exact orbit-plus-gain semantics and rejecting any internal Hamiltonian cycle or loss of smooth C4 order. Determine whether any splice preserves a functional 18-state transducer, creates a smaller permutation group, or introduces genuine set-valued gain branching. If branching appears, freeze the smallest explicit control; if a permutation survives, iterate and compile its group backbone before considering larger networks.
